review_scope: Primary read the complete first-pass report and independently read the full env.json, task.json, controls.json, generator, browser JavaScript, mechanic CSS, grader, task verifier and solver. The shared verifier helper had already been read in full.
decision: Keep the baseline labels and L1 reasoning/planning No exception. Functional platform heights, one-way lower-platform landings and held movement support 3D and temporal labels. Baseline side shelves create consequential route choices; L1 removes the branching choice. The forward descending route and marked exit are available as visible geometry, without a required information-reveal or interface-learning stage.

rationale_clarifications.exploration_interface: Do not generalize the first-pass statement that looking around never counts as exploration: active viewing does count when it reveals information needed to solve. Here the generator starts the camera toward the next terrace and lays the route ahead, while the renderer exposes platform tops, sides and the exit marker. Camera alignment can support navigation, but there is no supported necessity for a separate search or probe before choosing the visible forward continuation. This is not based merely on all platform data being present in the renderer.

additional_source_evidence.claim: Route terrace centers advance along one horizontal axis; the initial camera heading points toward the next terrace.
Both interfaces sustain movement across ticks and require release/redirection; discrete look buttons do not turn held walking into an untimed action.

uncertainties: Source review only; this does not establish screenshot-only agent performance or visual legibility at every viewpoint and seed.
